speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Chalk at the head of the board. Pence in the right-hand column, where they cannot run into the shillings.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: I keep the pence on the right already. The dozen is what tangles, when a thing is counted by the dozen and then said in shillings.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Turn every dozen into shillings before thou addest a line. Twelve at fourpence is four shillings. Write the four shillings. Wipe the twelve out of thy head.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Four shillings. That is an example. We did not buy twelve of anything this morning.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: It is an example. Nothing left the house for it. Again. Six pair at sevenpence.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Three shillings and sixpence. Together with the four, seven shillings and sixpence.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Keep a notch on a stick all the same. Chalk wipes off with an elbow. A notch stays until someone means it to go.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Thy grandfather could tell a skin by the cut of a thumb-nick, and his stories grow a penny between Whitsun and harvest. Cast the story. Do not correct him at the table.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: He said four-and-twenty pair at the May fair, sixteen shillings, and ninepence the pair. Four-and-twenty at ninepence is eighteen shillings, not sixteen.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then the pair in the story was eightpence, or the sixteen was a tale. Cast it, and leave it on the slate.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: The pair was eightpence. It has grown a penny in the telling. Thou wilt not tell him so while he is in the middle of it.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Check the sum. Keep thy tongue. Dinner is not a correction of thy grandfather.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: I am not telling him. I am telling the slate.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Now the Monday list. Cast the salt, from the fair copy, not from memory.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Bay for the tub, and a peck of the white. And the two bushels, with the four struck. I can read the hand, and I can see the letter Grandmother put back.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Leave the list under the weight when you are done. The letter does not need to be said aloud to stay in the word.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Wash the chalk off thy fingers before the cloth.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Three columns, and the bottom comes out even. Nothing in the columns was bought today.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Cleanly cast. The examples can be wiped. The list stays.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: Wipe the examples. Do not wipe the two bushels. They were enough argument for one week.

speaker: susanna_shakespeare
text: Wiped. The two stays in my head, and the twelve-at-fourpence does not, because it was never ours.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Good. A slate is not a purse.

speaker: mary_shakespeare
text: Eightpence on the slate, and ninepence in his mouth. Leave him the penny. He is in the middle of the story.

speaker: anne_shakespeare
text: And neither figure left the house. The bag at the door is not this slate.

speaker: william_shakespeare
text: Then we are done. The examples are gone. The two bushels are not.
